sections.h2: Where is the Davidson County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office sits in the Public Square Garage at 300 Deaderick Street, Nashville, TN 37201. Staff are at the counter from 8:00 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon on weekdays, and the main number is 615-862-6790. Letters go to Post Office Box 196398, Nashville, TN 37219-6398, but a courier other than the U.S. Postal Service must use the street address.

This is where Davidson County keeps its warranty deeds, deeds of trust, releases, powers of attorney, liens and plats. If you sell a house anywhere in the county, the deed your buyer signs ends up on these shelves, and so does the paper that clears your old mortgage.

Davidson County is unusual in Tennessee because the city and the county have shared one government since 1963, called Metro Nashville. The register is a Metro department, so its pages live on nashville.gov beside the other Metro offices.

sections.h2: What does a seller get from the Davidson County register's app and online tools?
sections.html:
The register offers a free mobile app, listed in the Apple and Google stores as Nashville - Davidson Co. ROD, that puts several office services on a phone. It includes a fee calculator, buttons to call or email the staff, and the Property Alert sign-up.

Property Alert is worth a minute of a seller's time. It emails you if any document is filed under your name, which gives an early warning if someone tries to record a forged deed against your house. Many sellers only think about fraud after a closing goes wrong, and the sign-up is free.

  • Fee calculator for recording charges, on the office website and in the app
  • Property Alert email notices for filings under your name
  • Thank a Veteran program, which gives veterans a list of businesses offering discounts; veterans record their DD214 papers with the office in person
  • Online searching of recorded documents by subscription

The office's own FAQ says the staff will not draw up a deed, because a deed is a legal document and an attorney should prepare it. It also will not run a title search to tell you about liens, though the indexes are on public computers for anyone to use.

sections.h2: What are the charges for a Davidson County deed copy?
sections.html:
An uncertified copy of a recorded deed runs fifty cents a page and a certified one runs a dollar. Those rates hold at the counter and by post, though postal requests have a two-dollar floor.

Copy charges at the Davidson County Register of Deeds
ItemChargeHow to get it
Uncertified copy$0.50 per pageIn person or by mail
Certified copy$1 per pageIn person or by mail
Mailed request$2 minimumWritten request with a stamped return envelope and payment
Subdivision plat by mail$5Written request
Large plat copy in person$3Counter service

Source: Davidson County Register of Deeds, copies of deeds and documents. In person the office takes cash, checks, credit cards and money orders. A faxed copy is $1 a page, but only for customers who have opened an escrow account with the office first.

When you write for a copy, give the property address. If you want something other than a property deed, send as many details as you can so staff can find it in the indexes.

sections.h2: What gets a Nashville deed turned away at the counter?
sections.html:
The register decides only whether a paper can be accepted for recording, and leaves the question of legal soundness to the lawyer who drafted it. The University of Tennessee's county advisory staff lists what a deed must carry.

  • Legible text with a notarized acknowledgment, since the office's FAQ says every signature is notarized
  • Names and addresses for the owner and the taxpayer, under Tennessee Code section 66-24-114
  • A derivation clause that cites the earlier recorded deed, section 66-24-110
  • The drafter's name and address, section 66-24-115
  • The parcel number, section 66-24-122
  • Fees and any transfer tax due on the day it is filed

Davidson's register takes originals only. A certified copy of something already recorded with another government office is the single exception. When a deed calls for an oath of consideration, that oath gets its own notary stamp. Leaving off the parcel number or the preparer's name is a quick way to have a recording refused, so ask the closing attorney to read the list against your deed ahead of the signing.

sections.h2: What transfer tax does a Nashville sale trigger?
sections.html:
Tennessee levies 37 cents on every $100 of the sale price as a realty transfer tax. The Department of Revenue explains that the buyer, as grantee, hands it to the register along with the deed. A separate mortgage tax of 11.5 cents per $100 of debt applies to a new loan, after the first $2,000, and the borrower bears it.

According to the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimate, $417,400 is the median value of an owned home in this county. Multiplied out at the state rate, that is $1,544.38. The tax follows the actual price or market value on your deed, so your own contract number is the one that counts.

The state also says an exempt transfer needs no oath of value. The county training guide names transfers that end a tenancy by the entirety, divisions of land held in common, and leasehold estates among the exempt kinds.

sections.h2: What is Davidson County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Davidson County was created in 1783 and named for General William Lee Davidson of North Carolina. Its 526 square miles hold 504 of land, and the Cumberland River cuts through the middle from east to west. Metropolitan Nashville Public Schools serves every address in the county, and a handful of small cities that incorporated before consolidation kept their own governments.

Census QuickFacts describe a market with a very different mix from the state's smaller counties:

  • 745,904 people in the July 2025 estimate, against 715,887 at the 2020 base
  • 52.8 percent owner-occupied, so close to half of households rent
  • Typical rent of $1,582 a month and typical household income of $77,853
  • 389,379 housing units and 5,632 building permits in 2025

About 15 percent of residents were born abroad, and 48.4 percent of those 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. A seller with a dated or inherited house here faces a large pool of renters and newcomers, and a cash sale is one route to weigh against a listing.

sections.h2: Where does recording leave a Nashville seller on the tax bill?
sections.html:
Recording changes the name on the public record and has no effect on what is owed. Property tax follows the January 1 assessment, comes due on the first Monday of October, and turns delinquent once February ends, per the Comptroller's calendar.

Before you close, ask the Metropolitan Trustee what stands against your parcel. The trustee keeps weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Disputes over value start with the equalization board for the county and can move on to the State Board of Equalization, which takes appeals until August 1 or until 45 days after the local board's notice, whichever is later.

Owners who are 65 or disabled may receive state tax relief on up to $33,600 of value if income stayed at or under $38,470. Applications go through the trustee.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in Davidson County?
faqs.a: The Davidson County Register of Deeds records them, from the Public Square Garage at 300 Deaderick Street in Nashville. Call 615-862-6790. The office holds deeds, deeds of trust, releases, liens and plats.

faqs.q: Will the register take a photocopy of my deed?
faqs.a: Only a certified copy of something already recorded with another government office. Everything else has to be an original, signed and notarized.

faqs.q: What does a recorded deed copy cost in Davidson County?
faqs.a: Fifty cents a page plain and a dollar a page certified. Mailed requests cost at least $2, and a mailed subdivision plat is $5.

faqs.q: Can the Davidson County register tell me about liens on my house?
faqs.a: No. Staff say a lien search takes a title search by an attorney or title company, although the indexes are open to the public on office computers. The office does not write deeds.

faqs.q: How do I get a warning if someone files a deed in my name?
faqs.a: Sign up for Property Alert, a free register of deeds service that sends an email when any document is filed under your name. It is available on the office website and in the mobile app.
